changes.before: Remove using Study but change Session to Study.Session everywhere it appears in Main. What happens?
changes.after: Use a namespace to organize a type's name.

before: A namespace groups types so different areas can use similar short names without collision. Study.Session below belongs to the Study namespace.
using Study permits the short name Session. It does not install a package or add a project reference. A namespace and an assembly are different concepts.

These examples usually use top-level statements. This example instead puts its starting statements inside public static void Main() in Program. Main is the explicit entry point; static means no Program instance is needed.

A .csproj specifies how a project is built. To use a type from another project, add a project reference as well as any desired using directive. This example keeps both namespaces in one project; separate files are optional.
Expected behavior from this example: 12. This expected result is a reasoned prediction until a compiler test is recorded.

Optional local transfer: Move Session into a second source file in the same project. Then explore a class-library project reference separately; a using directive alone will not create that reference. This is a separate local practice task, not a requirement to mark the reading complete.
after: A namespace groups related types under a name. It helps prevent clashes when different parts of a program use the same short type name.
Study.Session is the full name of the Session record in the Study namespace. The dot separates the namespace from the type name.
using Study lets this file write Session as a short name. It does not install code or create a link to another project.
This program starts in Program.Main instead of top-level statements. Main is the entry point, where execution begins. static means no Program object is needed to call it.
The program prints 12. Main creates a Session with 12 minutes and prints that property.

A .csproj file describes how a project is built. Using code from another project requires a project reference. An assembly is a compiled code unit; it is different from the namespaces that organize names inside code.

before.question: Remove using Study but change Session to Study.Session everywhere it appears in Main. What happens?
choices: It still prints 12 because the name is fully qualified
before.explanation: Fully qualifying the type names its namespace explicitly. The using directive only provided a convenient shorter spelling.

after.question: Remove using Study and write Study.Session in both places in Main. What happens?
after.explanation: The full type name identifies Session directly. using only allowed the shorter spelling.
